questions.q: Which orbitals are mixed to form $sp$ hybrid orbitals?
options: One s orbital and two p orbitals
One s orbital and one p orbital
One s orbital and three p orbitals
questions.explain: This hybridization process involves mixing of the valence s orbital with one of the valence p orbitals to yield two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[2](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F7-6-molecular-structure-and-polarity)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)][[4](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-4-molecular-orbital-theory)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)

questions.q: In the linear molecule $BeCl_2$, what is the hybridization of the central Beryllium atom?
questions.explain: The beryllium atom in a gaseous $BeCl_2$ molecule exhibits $sp$ hybridization, corresponding to two regions of electron density.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)

questions.q: The Boron atom in $BH_3$ has a trigonal planar geometry. What is its hybridization?
questions.explain: The trigonal planar structure suggests $sp^2$ hybridization, resulting from the mixing of one s orbital and two p orbitals. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: What hybridization is exhibited by the carbon atom in methane ($CH_4$)?
questions.explain: The carbon atom in methane exhibits $sp^3$ hybridization, forming four identical orbitals directed to the corners of a tetrahedron.[[1](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fchem.libretexts.org%2FBookshelves%2FGeneral_Chemistry%2FMap%253A_Chemistry_-_The_Central_Science_(Brown_et_al.)%2F11%253A_Liquids_and_Intermolecular_Forces%2F11.02%253A_Intermolecular_Forces)][[3](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fopenstax.org%2Fbooks%2Fchemistry-2e%2Fpages%2F8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)] [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Phosphorus pentachloride ($PCl_5$) has five bonding pairs. Which set of hybrid orbitals is used?
questions.explain: We use the 3s orbital, the three 3p orbitals, and one of the 3d orbitals to form the set of five $sp^3d$ hybrid orbitals. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)
questions.subject: Chemistry

questions.q: Which hybridization allows Sulfur in $SF_6$ to bond to six fluorine atoms?
questions.explain: To bond six fluorine atoms, the 3s orbital, the three 3p orbitals, and two of the 3d orbitals form six equivalent $sp^3d^2$ hybrid orbitals. [Source: OpenStax](https://openstax.org/books/chemistry-2e/pages/8-2-hybrid-atomic-orbitals)
